youtube.title: A POLITICAL AGENDA
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke is joined by Joel Rowlands, former Opportunity Party candidate, and independent journalist Chantelle Baker to discuss NZ First’s proposed tougher sentencing for child rapists, allegations that the Opportunity Party has become a corporate, network-driven operation and the prospects of a grand coalition. The panel also examines politicians’ engagement with gangs, lingering anger over COVID-era decisions, unrest in France, immigration and New Zealand’s changing identity. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday and find out everything about the overhang, wasted vote and tactical voting at Vote Smart Find Joel on Facebook and Chantelle on Facebook

youtube.title: ERIKA HARVEY & KIRSTEN MURFITT
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan is joined by Erika Harvey of Lobby for Good and Tauranga lawyer Kirsten Murfitt to discuss the Auditor-General’s findings about the sale of the city’s Marine Precinct for just under $14 million. They challenge the findings, question the deal’s value for ratepayers and describe their efforts to scrutinise council property transactions. Find more from Kirsten at KM Law or follow Kirsten Murfitt on Facebook For more on Erika, visist Erika Harvey website , Lobby For Good or find Lobby for Good on X

youtube.title: DON BRASH & MATT ROBSON
youtube.summary: Don Brash and Matthew Robson rejoin Paul Brennan to debate New Zealand’s rising debt, the cost of an ageing population and competing approaches to economic growth. They question closer military alignment with the United States, warn against expanding online censorship powers and discuss the need for early intervention to prevent crime. Despite their political differences, both argue for greater scrutiny of government policy and more informed public debate. youtube.summary: Join Claire Deeks and Alia Bland for RCR’s Lolly Scramble webinar. A relaxed, informative look at MMP, strategic voting, overhangs and “wasted” votes. youtube.title: RCR contributor Lisa Spencer speaks to Australian political commentator Hugo Lennon
youtube.summary: RCR contributor Lisa Spencer speaks to Australian nationalist activist and political commentator Hugo Lennon about how he became involved in nationalism at the British Australian Community Political Action Conference.

youtube.title: JAN RIVERS
youtube.summary: Jan Rivers, spokeswoman for Genspect New Zealand and Public Good, discusses the High Court’s ruling on the government’s puberty blocker restrictions. She argues that the case focused on consultation and legal process rather than a full assessment of the medical evidence and says opposing perspectives were given insufficient weight. With prescriptions continuing and an appeal being sought, Jan says that the debate over children’s welfare and future policy is far from over. For more from Jan visit Public Good & Genspect or find Jan on X and Substack

youtube.title: MEDIA MATTERS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Marty Gibson examine the Chris Luxon–Chris Hipkins debate, arguing that the major parties are increasingly alike and questioning media criticism of MMP’s overhang strategy. They discuss New Zealand’s rising government debt, proposed social media controls and Green and Te Pāti Māori MPs’ engagement with gangs, debating how to address gang crime without romanticising it or ignoring its victims. youtube.title: MICHAEL LAWS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan chats with Michael Laws, Otago Regional Councillor and New Zealand First candidate for Waitaki, about the erosion of public trust, which he traces to Rogernomics and the rise of economic liberalism. Michael argues that powerful elites and cartels disadvantage ordinary New Zealanders, calls for university reform, discusses the Treaty of Waitangi and social division and warns that National’s two-tick strategy could hand the election to the centre-left. For more on Michael Laws or find him on Facebook For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday and find out everything about the overhang, wasted vote and tactical voting at Vote Smart

youtube.title: MARK KAPLAN
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan interviews Health Truth founder Mark Kaplan, whose heart attack at 52 prompted him to question conventional approaches to chronic disease. Mark explains his vision for Neo, an AI-powered health platform designed to analyse personal health data, connect users with doctors and challenge pharmaceutical influence. They discuss root-cause health, nutrition, metabolic disease and the goal of extending healthspan rather than simply lifespan. For more information: Visit the HealthTruth website or check out Neo Root or Neo and the Unplugged Movement Find Mark on X
